note: Adapted from Emerson’s 1952 original English description; the measurement tables (Tables 21 and 22 of the original) are interleaved with the plate captions in the scan and cannot be aligned line by line, so only the population mean head widths given in the text are retained here, and the full tables are not listed. The original did not describe the worker.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is distinguished from the other known alates of the genus by the combination of dark smoky wings, head width, eye diameter, ocellus size and hind tibia length; the postclypeus is similar to that of C. walkeri. Soldier labral lateral corners blunt and rounded, the margin between the base of the white median lobe and the lateral corners convex; it differs from C. acignathus and C. walkeri in the labrum (Fig. 14D) and the mandibles (Fig. 15F). Mean soldier head width differs considerably between populations (2.59 mm in various parts of Guyana, 3.07 mm at Itabu Creek, 3.12 mm at Manaos, 2.85 mm at Cachuela Esperanza, 2.63 mm at other Bolivian localities), possibly a sign of subspecific differentiation, but the material is insufficient and no subdivision is made for now.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Frontal gland plate concolorous with the head; pronotum slightly paler in the middle than at the margins; tibiae slightly darker than the femora; wing scales dark brown; wing membrane dark smoky brown, anterior margin and radius dark brown; sternites paler in the middle than at the sides. Head with a few setae; pronotum and wing scales with more setae than the head; tergites with setae and very few short hairs; sternites with setae and hairs. Frontal gland plate large, oval, dark, slightly raised above the head surface, convex. Eyes proportionally medium-sized, separated from the lower margin of the head by about 1/3—1/5 of their diameter. Ocelli as large as the frontal gland plate or smaller, separated from the eyes by about their own length to nearly 2 times their length, their upper margin raised above the head surface. Antennae 15-segmented, segment 3 sometimes partly divided. Postclypeus much less than half as long as wide. Sides of the pronotum strongly narrowed posteriorly, posterior margin concave. Within a population the male is usually smaller than the female.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head, pronotum and abdomen pale yellow, the head and labrum darker than the abdomen. Head sparsely covered with setae, with a few short hairs below; postmentum with a few short hairs in the middle and about 2 long setae at the front; pronotum with a few setae and short hairs on the anterior margin; tergites with setae; sternites with setae and short hairs. Sides of the head slightly curved, narrowed anteriorly. Frontal tube rather short, upturned, just reaching the base of the postclypeus from above; the base of the frontal tube is wider in Bolivian specimens than in Brazilian and Guyanese specimens. Narrowest part of the postmentum about 2/5 of the greatest width. Antennae 15-segmented. Lateral corners of the labrum blunt and rounded, the margin between the base of the white median lobe and the lateral corners convex. Anterior margin of the pronotum weakly to distinctly concave.
